correctness.rationale: PASS: The displayed real 4×4 matrix was checked symbolically to be orthogonal. The two input Fock components are normalized and mutually orthogonal. For each output with exactly one q=1 photon at i∈{1,2,3}, independent symbolic expansion gives amplitude (1+e^{iφ})/12; three orthogonal internal-resolved outcomes yield (1+cosφ)/24. The incoherent mixture gives 1/24 and φ=π gives zero. Relevant two-photon amplitudes √2/4 and 1/(2√3), and fully indistinguishable three-photon amplitude √6/8, are nonzero. This verifies suppression produced by coherence in the arbitrary internally correlated state, not independent-product sources.

value.rationale: PASS: A small exact counterexample isolates a missing hypothesis in a published arbitrary-input mathematical conjecture. Its phase-only change switches an exact 3-photon output from 1/12 to zero while every fully indistinguishable subset transition remains nonzero. It clarifies a rigorous boundary between correlated and independent preparations; no broad theorem about arbitrary products is claimed.

final_claim: For the explicit real 4-port interferometer and normalized coherent fixed-spatial-occupation (2,1,0,0) three-photon input, P(1,1,1,0)=(1+cosφ)/24, so a coherence-created zero at φ=π contradicts the unrestricted arbitrary-input conjecture without suppressed indistinguishable subsets.
